text: The Nationals Campaign Launch
The Hon Mark Vaile MP
Deputy Prime Minister
Leader of The Nationals
Campaign Launch Speech
An Experienced Team for Australia's Future
Brisbane
Australia today is a nation of confident and optimistic people.
It hasn’t always been that way.
In the past 11 years, that confidence and optimism has grown under the strong management of our Coalition Government.
In that time, Australians have come to feel more secure.
- More secure within our borders.
- More secure within our economy.
- More secure within their jobs.
Now that we have a strong economy; now that we have more people in full-time work than at any other time in Australia’s history, we need to lock it in.
An optimistic and confident Australia now needs a strong plan for the future
– and we need to keep our nation in safe hands.
Our strong plan includes aiming for a full employment economy.
An economy where every Australian who wants a job can get one.
Our strong plan is about guiding our nation through the challenges that lie ahead,
while helping all Australians to share in the opportunities and benefits that come from a well managed economy.
We must ensure that these opportunities and benefits are available to all Australians, including the 7.5 million people living outside our capital cities.
Better health care for rural and remote communities
We know that families across Australia want better health care.
In particular they want better services from their public hospital system.
I want to reiterate our commitment to appointing local hospital boards.
We want public hospitals to be controlled by men and women who know the hospital staff and know the patients and have a personal commitment to the health of their community.
Local boards will have more control of their hospitals, making it harder for State Labor Governments to downgrade hospital services in rural and regional areas.

While we will give control of hospitals back to local people, Labor wants to replace the state bureaucrats running hospitals with federal bureaucrats who would be even more remote from doctors, nurses, and their patients.
The Coalition Government has worked hard to attract medical professionals to rural and regional areas.
One of the impediments is sourcing relief locums when specialists need time off or time to upgrade their professional skills.
The Coalition Government has put a scheme in place to provide locums for specialist obstetricians in rural areas.
The scheme was due to end in 2009.

I am announcing today that we will extend the scheme into the future, because it has been highly successful in helping specialist obstetricians to stay in the country where they are needed and where they want to practice.
The Coalition will also provide extra training support for doctors in rural areas who carry out medical procedures.
I am announcing today that we will commit $15 million to establish a new Rural and Remote Medical Training Equipment Fund.

The funding will purchase and distribute training simulators and support equipment that will be used to train doctors to treat conditions that they may only see occasionally in the day to day operations of their practice.
This programme will allow rural GPs to keep their skills up to date
and help deliver better services for rural people.
A better education
One of the best ways we can spread Australia's prosperity is to make sure that every Australian student gets a good education, including vocational training or university after they leave school.
It's good for the individual and it’s good for the country: we need more people with technical and vocational skills in our economy.
A re-elected Coalition will deliver a core national curriculum.
We will deliver certainty and national standards that all schools must meet.
Australians don’t want a risky “education revolution”.
It sounds like something that might happen in a Communist country.
We will make sure opportunities exist in both the country and the city.
Students in remote areas don’t need a revolution – they just need a bit of help.
These students often face an insurmountable barrier to continuing their education; it’s the tyranny of distance.
Their families cannot afford the cost of sending them to live in a distant city to pursue educational opportunities.
A re-elected Coalition Government will help these families.

I am announcing today that we will provide 1,000 students per year in remote Australia with $4,000 bursaries to help them participate in higher education – either university or vocational education and training.
Students will have to apply for the bursaries; they will be allocated to the 1,000 students who need them most.
The Remote Students Bursary scheme will start on 1 July 2008.
This is a key part of our strong plan for ensuring all Australians share in the prosperity of the nation.
A more compassionate Australia
Our strong economic management has given us the ability to take on the great challenges that Australia is facing, including the drought.
The Coalition Government has now committed $3.5 billion in drought assistance, which is helping more than 40,000 farming families and small businesses.
We have the strong plan and the safe hands to maintain Australia's strong economy.
We will spread its benefits to every street and every family.
We will ensure we share our prosperity with the people who have built this nation.
That’s why we will increase the utilities allowance for older Australians to help meet basic household bills like power and gas.
For the first time we will extend the utilities allowance to carers and disability support pensioners
and double the senior’s concession allowance to help self-funded retirees with cost of living pressures.
Transport for Australia's future
Our strong plan for the future includes an integrated vision for improving local roads and national highways to meet our future transport needs.
We have now committed record amounts of funding:
- to fix the nation’s highways
- to fix the major urban road networks
- to fix the strategic regional roads network; and
- to fix the local roads network.
At last we can afford to invest in infrastructure that will drive growth and create jobs.
Our plan will develop a safe and efficient transport network:
- a network that is safe for mums and dads doing the school run.
- a network that allows our industries to efficiently move goods around the country,
- and at the same time eliminate millions of truck movements from our urban roads.
Many Australian families today are concerned about the rising cost of fuel.
It's not only a problem for families: it's a challenge for our whole country.
The vast size of this nation means everything we do – from driving to work, to moving our exports to port has a transport cost.
The Coalition believes that we need to source more of our fuel from crops grown in Australia.
We believe we should be using more green fuel in Australia.
We have made a good start but there is a lot more to be done.
Australia's production of biofuels is expected to increase from 106 million litres in 2006 to 217 million litres in 2007.
It is on track to reach the Government's production target, which is 350 million litres per year by 2010.
We need to make biofuels available to more Australians.
Today, I am announcing a strong plan to increase Australia's biofuel production and to encourage more Australians to choose biofuels at the fuel pump.

The number of service stations selling ethanol blended fuel has increased from 70 in 2005 – just after the Labor Party had demonised ethanol as a green fuel – now we have 800 outlets across the nation.
We want to see more.
A re-elected Coalition Government will extend the Ethanol Distribution Programme until June 2009.
We expect that an extra 400 service stations will take up the $20,000 grants to help convert to selling ethanol blended fuel.
The Coalition's biofuel plan is good news for the family budget, because ethanol blended fuel is about 3 cents per litre cheaper than ordinary unleaded petrol.
It's good news for Australia, because it reduces our dependence on imported fuel.
And it's good news for the environment, because it reduces our greenhouse gas emissions.

That is why today I am also announcing that a re-elected Coalition Government will commit a further $5 million to work with the biofuels industry to make more Australians aware of these benefits and to drive demand.
More research into second generation biofuels
At the moment, ethanol is produced from food crops like wheat, corn and sugar.
But the race is on to find a way to make ethanol in commercial quantities from plant waste like sugar cane bagasse, crop stubble, and sawmill residue.
It's called lignocellulosic ethanol.
The Coalition Government will continue to support research into these second generation biofuels, by providing $5 million to support further research and development.
The Coalition will also fund a $6 million trial to test whether biodiesel meets heavy vehicle diesel standards – a key step towards driving a future biodiesel industry.
Heavy vehicles account for 40 per cent of Australia's diesel consumption and the trial will test whether the B20 biodiesel blend can meet the diesel fuel standard.
Australia needs an experienced team with safe hands.
We have a strong plan for the future
and the safe, experienced hands to deliver it.
The case for the re-election of the Coalition Government is compelling.
We have established the strongest economic platform this nation has ever stood on – a $1.1 trillion economy.
We have established the strongest employment platform this nation has ever experienced – 10.5 million people in work.
We have had an unprecedented 16 years of continuous economic expansion.
The Coalition has a strong plan for the nation’s future.
What Australia needs now is the right leadership with safe hands to guide the nation forward.
